baseline.state: Sinkhorn topology is declared, arithmetically defined (wave 17, oracle-pinned stages), physically owned, semantically addressed and carried (wave 18), and execution refuses before traversal at PreparedOperands::load (prepared.rs:741). 44 HC tests pass. what_the_reconnaissance_already_changed: the residual add is the seam: expand_streams replaces `backend.residual_add` (carry + add are one op)
the pre-norm moves inside the branch and normalises the reduced vector, not the bundle
sublayer_forward does not drop into the batch path: stages 1-3 per position, operator over the batch, stage 5 per position
no existing tap can witness the path; the witness state is the split and the reduced vector

the_transition.intervention: Change the residual carrier from one `[hidden]` vector to an explicit hyper-connection bundle across hyper-connected transformer layers, reducing to `[hidden]` only at ordinary operator boundaries and expanding back into the bundle at the two HC sites.
the_transition.success: An independent intermediate-state witness proves the wave-17 HC operation actually ran, in decode AND batch traversal; ordinary operator dispatch is unchanged; headless layer traversal works; single-stream traversal stays byte-identical; only then do the traversal refusals lift.
the_transition.non_claim: No DeepSeek base-dialect work, no K3 AttnRes work, no representation work (no new role, placement or schema), no real-payload claim, no explanation of GLM's `mhc`.

the_four_decisions.1_carrier: The traversal state becomes a bundle; `hidden` does not change meaning. decode: `[streams, hidden]`; batch: `[positions, streams, hidden]`. Every ordinary operation keeps consuming `[hidden]` / `[positions, hidden]`. The topology dimension and the model width are different semantic dimensions and are never flattened into a pretend wider residual at an API boundary: wherever a plane, trace row or resume row crosses a boundary for an HC plan it is typed as a bundle (streams × hidden), and validated as such.
the_four_decisions.2_composition_owner: Traversal owns SEQUENCING. `exec::hyper_connection` owns TOPOLOGY ARITHMETIC and gains the site-level composition: `reduce(bundle, site) -> (split, v)` and `update(bundle, branch_out, split) -> bundle'`. The backend keeps owning the ordinary operator. Neither mix_projection nor the Sinkhorn split appears in operator dispatch. `sublayer_forward` stays as the single-position reference composition; the decode path may call it directly. Invariant: wave 19 changes the residual carrier and traversal sequencing; it does not change what attention or FFN means. The hybrid FFN's raw-residual reads receive v_ffn, never the bundle.
the_four_decisions.3_refusals: No reader lifts early. Order: bundle traversal implemented -> intermediate witness exists -> witness mutation-tested -> decode traversal proven -> batch traversal proven -> shared execution authority lifts (executor, report, encode admission move TOGETHER) -> the independent plan/semantics table is reconciled and scored SEPARATELY. Traversal is not CLOSED after decode alone. The wave splits into 19a and 19b with the global refusal intact after 19a.
the_four_decisions.4_substrate: A new finite synthetic container at hidden 5 whose geometry agrees with the untouched wave-17 oracle (streams 4, hidden 5, mix rows 24, iters 20, eps 1e-6), with deterministic finite operand values — never the pattern-byte fixture. Its HC site operands ARE the oracle's weights. The oracle is not adapted.

19a_decode.delivers: bundle carrier on the decode path; `exec::hyper_connection::{reduce, update}` composition; the hidden-5 substrate (headless and head-bearing variants; a hybrid-FFN variant for mutant d); the HC site trace on the decode observer; the witness; the mutation tests; a crate-internal preparation seam used only by the witness (the doctored-seam pattern encode_graph already sets), so the PUBLIC refusal at PreparedOperands::load is untouched.
19a_decode.does_not_deliver: no batch traversal, no plane/resume/CLI width change, no reader lifts, no fixture migration, no semantics-version bump.

19b_batch_and_lift.delivers: bundle carrier on the batch path (stages 1-3 per position, operator over the batch, stage 5 per position); the HC site trace on the plane sink; decode-vs-batch parity on the HC container; bundle-typed planes, resume rows and CLI plane persistence; the head reduction at the exit when declared; the headless whole-stack refusal; removal of the 19a seam; the shared authority lifts (readers 1, 2, 4 together); the semantics table reconciled; fixture migration; semantics version 15 -> 16.

the_witness.substrate: hidden 5, 4 streams, 2 layers, 3 positions with DISTINCT hidden states (the oracle's x has per-stream scales 0.1/1/3/7 and per-position variation), deterministic finite values, HC site operands = oracle weights (hc_fn 24x20, hc_base 24, hc_scale 3), head variant = oracle head weights (head_fn 4x20, head_base 4, head_scale). Ordinary operands (attention, FFN, norms, embedding, output) deterministic finite; their correctness is owned by single-stream byte-identity, not by this witness.
the_witness.entry_for_the_foreign_comparison: The oracle's input x `[3, 4, 5]` enters layer 0 as a bundle through the layer-range contract (a ResumePoint whose rows are bundles), so the attention site's stages see EXACTLY the oracle's state. The embedding entry cannot produce it (expand_embedding replicates streams), which is why the foreign comparison lives at the layer-range entry and the embedding entry is checked structurally.
the_witness.trace: one record per (layer, site ∈ {attn, ffn}, position): the Sinkhorn split {pre, post, comb}, the reduced vector v, and the branch output b. The branch output is included because mutant (d) is only detectable by recomputing the FFN branch from v_ffn and comparing. A one-stream transformer cannot produce any of these accidentally.
assertions: A1 foreign: at layer 0 attention site, tapped mix/pre/post/comb/reduced equal the oracle's stages within the wave-17 TOLERANCE, at all 3 positions

A2 structural: tapped bundle' == expand_streams(b_tapped, x, split_tapped) within TOLERANCE, and differs from x + b by more than TOLERANCE at every position (the oracle's single_stream_residual control disagrees)
A3 branch input: the existing attention-input tap equals pre_attention(v_tapped), not pre_attention(any stream) nor pre_attention(mean of streams)
A4 FFN site: b_ffn_tapped == the reference backend's FFN recomputed from v_ffn (residual argument = v_ffn) — on the hybrid variant this pins the router's input
A5 width: every HC-plan plane/trace row is a bundle of streams x hidden; every single-stream plane is `[hidden]` and byte-identical to baseline

A6 headless: LayerRange on the headless variant runs and yields a bundle; Full on the headless variant refuses at preparation with a reason naming the absent head, distinct from the topology reason; Full on the head-bearing variant produces `[hidden]` after head_reduce and logits
A7 parity: decode and batch produce bit-identical HC traces and logits on the reference backend
mutants_each_must_be_caught_before_any_r: (a) bypass the HC composition (run the layer single-stream on stream 0) -> A5 (width) and A1 (no split emitted)
(b) wrong split or reduction (1 Sinkhorn iteration; uniform pre; transposed comb) -> A1 at the split, A2 at the expansion
(c) pre-norm on the original residual / a stream / the stream mean instead of v -> A3
(d) bundle or wrong stream as the hybrid FFN's raw residual -> A4
(e) batch only: apply position 0's split to every row -> A1 at positions 1 and 2, A7
the_witness.glm_constraint_hard: No `hc_head_*` is needed anywhere inside a layer or a LayerRange. `head_reduce` runs only after the whole hyper-connected stack and only when a head is declared.

falsifiers: A1 fails at any position -> the traversal fed the site the wrong state or bound the wrong operand; do not proceed to 19b
any mutant survives -> the witness is not a witness; the refusal stays and the witness is redesigned before any capability claim
A7 not bit-identical -> decode and batch compose differently; resolve before any reader lifts
any single-stream test changes by one bit -> the carrier leaked into the single-stream program
P7 GLM reads 30 on reader 2 -> a hyper-connected component with no head was reported executable: fail-open, a BUG
P8 retiring the table moves a row other than the three HC rows, or fails to move one of them -> the table encoded something other than 'traversal unsupported' and needs its own finding
the hidden-5 substrate cannot be entered with the oracle's x through the layer-range contract -> the entry contract is the wrong witness shape; record it, do not widen the contract silently
how_this_wave_can_be_wrong_in_a_way_the_: Only stages 1-3 have a foreign reference through the traversal (A1). Stage 5 and the FFN site are checked by recomputation with this build's own stage functions and reference backend (A2, A4): a shared misreading of the reference that the wave-17 stage tests did not already catch would pass both.
Decode and batch will share the composition helper, so A7 cannot see a bug they share; A1 is the only check that stands outside both.

The hidden-5 container's ordinary operands have no external reference; single-stream byte-identity covers the operators but not the specific numbers, so an FFN-site error that is symmetric under the mutants listed would pass.
Storage orientation and dtype of hc_fn on a real checkpoint (DeepSeek F32, GLM BF16) are untested until the real-weight witness; this wave says nothing about them.
